_comment: English is the SCHEMA, not just a translation: every lookup falls back here, and a
key absent from this file does not exist as far as the app is concerned. Adding a
string means adding it here first; tests/test_i18n.py then names it as untranslated
in every other catalog until someone fills it in.
Values are PLAIN TEXT -- never markup. Jinja autoescapes t() and the browser side
assigns through textContent, so a tag in here renders as visible angle brackets.
Placeholders are {named}, and the set of names in a translation must match this
file's exactly (a test enforces it -- a dropped {machine} is a silent bug).
Keys are dotted paths written as nested objects, so a 500-key file stays reviewable.
The leading section is the page or component the string belongs to; 'common' is for
text that genuinely appears on several pages, not a dumping ground.

_language_auto: The topbar picker's first option, and the label for the same choice in Settings.
Means 'I have not chosen -- follow my browser', which is what a user is put back

_shell: The app shell -- the sidebar/topbar document that stays put while pages load into a
frame inside it (see app.py's _shell_mode). frame_title names that frame for screen
readers, which announce an untitled frame as nothing more useful than 'frame'.

login.title: Sign in
login.prompt: Sign in with an authorized account to view the dashboard.

denied.title: Access denied
denied.default_message: You do not have permission to view this page.
denied.note: Permissions come from the groups you belong to. Ask an administrator to add you to a group that covers this.

dashboard.heading: Live CPU Monitor
dashboard.empty: No machines have reported in yet.

_resolution_label: The four bucket sizes a machine's history charts can be aggregated at. 'Raw' is prose and needs
translating; the other three are duration abbreviations, so translate them only if
your language abbreviates seconds/minutes differently. The VALUES sent to the API
are fixed strings ('raw', '10s', ...) and are not these labels.

inventory.heading: Asset Inventory
inventory.intro: Every machine that is, or ever was, visible to the hub. Online machines also appear on the live Dashboard; offline ones stay here until deleted. Deleting a machine permanently removes its identity, temperature history, and fleet enrollment.
inventory.search_placeholder: Search name, manufacturer, asset tag, serial, service tag…
inventory.empty: No machines have reported in yet.
inventory.confirm_delete:
Permanently delete "{machine}"?

This removes its identity, all temperature history, and its fleet enrollment. This cannot be undone.
inventory.wake_all_title: Ask an awake PC on each subnet to wake the PCs that are switched off.
inventory.wake_all_result: Asked for {count} PCs to be woken.
inventory.wake_all_none: Every PC you can see is already awake.
inventory.wake_all_failed: Could not request a fleet-wide wake.

alerts.heading: Alerts
alerts.intro: Conditions that want your attention. Machines running hot — whose average temperature over the configured window is at or above the high-temperature threshold — show here and stay until you dismiss them, one card per episode, so a machine that runs hot repeatedly builds up a card per spell rather than replacing the last one. So do duplicate machines that share a serial number while both are online: the hub won't merge live machines automatically, so pick which record to keep and the others are merged into it (their temperature history is preserved).
alerts.empty: No open alerts. You're all caught up.

high_temp.title: High temperature: {machine}
_window: A sentence fragment, not a string of its own: it fills {window} in the four
bodies below so a known window reads '5-min average' and an unknown one reads
'windowed average'. Translate it as it would appear mid-sentence.
high_temp.ongoing: The {window} average {avg} °C is at or above the {threshold} °C threshold. Hot since {since}.
high_temp.ongoing_peak: The {window} average {avg} °C is at or above the {threshold} °C threshold (peak {peak} °C). Hot since {since}.
high_temp.ended: Ran at or above the {threshold} °C threshold. From {from} until {until}.
high_temp.ended_peak: Ran at or above the {threshold} °C threshold, peaking at {peak} °C ({window} average). From {from} until {until}.

duplicate.title: ⚠ Duplicate serial number: {serial}
duplicate.intro: These machines report the same serial and are both online. Choose the record to keep:
duplicate.pick_first: Pick a machine to keep first.

confirm.one:
Keep "{survivor}" and merge "{victim}" into it?

The merged machines' temperature history moves onto "{survivor}"; their duplicate records and fleet enrollments are removed. This cannot be undone.
confirm.other:
Keep "{survivor}" and merge {count} machines into it?

The merged machines' temperature history moves onto "{survivor}"; their duplicate records and fleet enrollments are removed. This cannot be undone.

audit.heading: Audit Log
audit.intro: Who did what on this hub: every command issued, machine changed, package deployed, account edited, and key touched. Append-only and not machine-scoped — entries are never rewritten or deleted, so this is the record to reach for after the fact.
audit.empty_filtered: No audit entries match these filters.

showing_recent.one: Showing the {count} most recent matching entry.
showing_recent.other: Showing the {count} most recent matching entries.

audit.load_failed: Could not load the audit log: {error}

users.heading: Users
users.intro: The people who use this console. Anyone who signs in is added automatically; you can also add someone ahead of their first login. Editing a profile here does not change what they can do — that is set by their Permission Groups.
users.search_placeholder: Search by name, username, or email
users.empty_hint: Anyone who signs in appears here automatically.
users.confirm_delete:
Remove "{user}" from the directory?

This only removes their profile. It does NOT change what they can do or whether they can sign in — that is set by their Permission Groups.

permissions.heading: Permission Groups
permissions.intro: A group grants a set of capabilities over a set of machines. A person's effective access is the union of every group they belong to.
_breakglass: {allowed_emails} is the name of a .env key and is passed in verbatim -- it is a
configuration key, not a word, so it must not be translated. It is a placeholder
rather than part of the sentence so it cannot be translated by accident.
permissions.breakglass: Addresses in {allowed_emails} are break-glass superusers: they hold every capability over every machine regardless of the groups below, and they can always sign in. That is what lets you create the first group here, and what stops a mistake on this page from locking everyone out. Everyone else must be in a group to sign in at all.
permissions.empty_hint: Until you create one, only the break-glass addresses above can sign in.
_directory_group_list: Appears under a group's members. {groups} is the comma-separated list of tokens;
the count is what is pluralised.
_confirm_delete: Two variants because a group can grant access by name AND through a mapped
directory group, and the warning has to name both. In the second, {members}
arrives ALREADY pluralised (from member_count below) so the sentence needs to
agree with only one count -- the same device history.meta uses.

confirm_delete.one:
Delete the permission group "{group}"?

{count} member loses the access it granted. Anyone left with no groups at all can no longer sign in.
confirm_delete.other:
Delete the permission group "{group}"?

{count} members lose the access it granted. Anyone left with no groups at all can no longer sign in.

confirm_delete_directory.one:
Delete the permission group "{group}"?

{members}, and anyone in {count} mapped directory group, lose the access it granted. Anyone left with no groups at all can no longer sign in.
confirm_delete_directory.other:
Delete the permission group "{group}"?

{members}, and anyone in {count} mapped directory groups, lose the access it granted. Anyone left with no groups at all can no longer sign in.

editor.name: Name
editor.scope_ad_ou: Machines in an Active Directory OU
editor.machine_placeholder: Search by name, asset tag, serial, service tag
editor.machine_empty: No matching machines — press Add to scope one that has not enrolled yet.
editor.ou_help: Machines are taken from Active Directory, and follow it: a PC moved into one of these OUs joins this group at the next directory sync, and one moved out leaves it. Nested OUs are included.
editor.ou_empty: No matching OUs — press Add to use exactly what you typed.
editor.ou_none_selected: No OUs selected — this group currently grants access to no machines.
editor.ou_no_machines: No machines are in these OUs yet. If Active Directory sync has not run since these PCs enrolled, they will appear after the next sync.
editor.member_placeholder: Search registered users, or type an email
editor.member_empty: No matching users — press Add to invite this email.
editor.directory_help: Anyone whose sign-in provider says they are in one of these groups gets this permission group, without being listed above by name. Paste the group's object ID (Entra), distinguished name, or name — whichever your provider sends. Membership is read once, at sign-in: a change in the directory takes effect the next time the person signs in.
editor.directory_add_token: Add this directory group to this permission group
editor.name_required: Enter a name to create this group.

_capability: One label + description per entry in permissions.CAPABILITIES. These are served by
GET /api/permissions/capabilities in the caller's language, so a capability with
no entry here would render its own key name in the group editor -- which is why
tests/test_i18n.py asserts the two sets match.

view.label: View
view.description: See these machines, their history, and their command results.

view_audit_log.label: View audit log
view_audit_log.description: Read the record of who did what on this hub. Security-sensitive entries are withheld unless the next capability is held too. The audit log is not machine-scoped.

view_security_audit.label: View security audit entries
view_security_audit.description: Additionally see security-level audit entries: permission changes, backup-key access, remote sessions, commands run, and settings changes. Does nothing without 'View audit log'.

issue_commands.label: Issue commands
issue_commands.description: Run scripts and send restart/shutdown/install commands. This is code execution as SYSTEM on the machines in scope.

manage_firmware.label: Manage firmware
manage_firmware.description: Change BIOS settings and update firmware. The only action with no way back: a failed firmware update can leave a machine unusable.

manage_settings.label: Manage settings
manage_settings.description: Change hub settings, and administer machine records (delete, merge, pin a sensor, dismiss alerts).

manage_users.label: Manage users
manage_users.description: Add, edit, and remove entries in the registered-users directory. This is a profile directory, not access -- membership in a permission group is what grants what someone can do.

manage_permission_groups.label: Manage permission groups
manage_permission_groups.description: Create and edit permission groups -- i.e. grant anyone, including themselves, any of the above.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.intro: Operational tuning for the hub and the fleet. Every setting shows its default, and anything you haven't changed behaves exactly as it did before this page existed.
_unit: Rendered as a suffix after a number input, and inside the range messages
("must be at least 60 seconds"). Keep them short -- they sit beside the input,
_field: One label -- plus help, plus a placeholder where the field has one -- per entry
in settings.REGISTRY. The key after `field.` IS the setting key, so a knob added
without entries here would render `settings.field.<key>.label` on the page;
tests/test_i18n.py asserts the two sets match. Help is one or two sentences shown
under the field, and is where the CONSEQUENCES of a knob belong -- an operator
reading it is deciding whether to change it.

computer.primary_sensor_preference.label: CPU temperature sensor preference
computer.primary_sensor_preference.help: Ordered, best first. The hub re-derives each machine's primary temperature from its reported sensor block, using the first name that matches. If none match, the temperature the agent picked is kept. Applies to new readings only -- history keeps the value recorded at the time.

hub.high_temp_threshold.label: High temperature threshold
hub.high_temp_threshold.help: When a machine's AVERAGE temperature over the window below is at or above this, a temperature alert is raised in the Alerts tab. The machine page also highlights a live reading at or above it.

hub.high_temp_avg_window_seconds.label: High temperature averaging window
hub.high_temp_avg_window_seconds.help: A machine is flagged as running hot only when its AVERAGE temperature over this window is at or above the threshold above, so a brief spike doesn't raise an alert. 300 = five minutes.

hub.low_load_threshold.label: Low-load threshold
hub.low_load_threshold.help: A high temperature recorded below this CPU load reads 'investigate' rather than 'expected' -- hot while idle is the interesting case.

hub.live_status_cache_seconds.label: Live status fallback age
hub.live_status_cache_seconds.help: After a hub restart the last known temperature and uptime are read back from the database. Past this age they are treated as unknown rather than shown as current.

hub.live_default_window_hours.label: Default chart window
hub.live_default_window_hours.help: How much history the live charts show before you pick a range.

hub.auto_update.label: Hub auto-update
hub.auto_update.help: Let the hub pull and apply its own updates from the main branch. Leave unset to follow HUB_AUTO_UPDATE in .env; set here to override that.

hub.default_language.label: Default console language
hub.default_language.help: The console language for anyone who has not picked one in the topbar. Automatic follows each person's browser. A personal choice always wins over this, so changing it does not override operators who have already chosen.

data.retention_days.label: Keep readings for
data.retention_days.help: Readings older than this are PERMANENTLY DELETED by the background pruner. Lowering this destroys history that cannot be recovered.

data.prune_interval_seconds.label: Run the pruner every
data.prune_interval_seconds.help: How often the retention pruner wakes up. Takes effect within 30 seconds, without a hub restart.

data.ingest_max_backdate_days.label: Accept backdated reports up to
data.ingest_max_backdate_days.help: An agent that was offline sends its buffered readings with their original timestamps; older than this they are treated as clock skew and stamped with the arrival time instead. Deliberately independent of the retention window -- shortening retention must not start silently flattening reconnect backfills.

data.command_output_retention_seconds.label: Keep terminal scrollback for
data.command_output_retention_seconds.help: Live terminal output is kept this long so you can scroll back. The durable command result is not affected.

metrics.collect_cpu_load.label: Record CPU load
metrics.collect_cpu_load.help: Chart CPU load % over time on the machine History dashboard.

metrics.collect_gpu.label: Record GPU temperature & load
metrics.collect_gpu.help: Chart discrete-GPU temperature and load. No effect on machines whose GPU reports nothing.

metrics.collect_disk.label: Record disk usage
metrics.collect_disk.help: Chart disk used-space % over time. The per-disk Storage cards are live readings and stay visible either way.

metrics.collect_disk_io.label: Record disk read/write
metrics.collect_disk_io.help: Chart disk read/write throughput (bytes per second, summed across all drives) over time.

metrics.collect_network.label: Record network throughput
metrics.collect_network.help: Chart network in/out (bytes per second). Also tells the agent whether to collect the network sensor category at all.

metrics.collect_fans.label: Record fan speed
metrics.collect_fans.help: Chart the fastest fan on the machine (RPM) over time. The per-fan Cooling cards are live readings and stay visible either way.

metrics.collect_power.label: Record CPU & GPU power
metrics.collect_power.help: Chart package power draw in watts. No effect on machines whose chips report no power sensor.

fleet.dashboard_online_window_seconds.label: Drop a machine off the Dashboard after
fleet.dashboard_online_window_seconds.help: A machine that hasn't reported a temperature within this window leaves the live Dashboard and reads as offline in Asset Inventory. Agents report every few seconds, so this tolerates a couple of missed reports without flapping.

fleet.offline_after_seconds.label: Mark an agent offline after
fleet.offline_after_seconds.help: Separate from the Dashboard window above: this is the command channel's view of whether an agent is reachable, used when you issue commands. Agents poll every 10 seconds.

fleet.command_ttl_seconds.label: Expire unclaimed commands after
fleet.command_ttl_seconds.help: A command not picked up by its target within this window expires instead of running much later on a machine that just came back.

deploy.default_max_attempts.label: Default attempts per machine
deploy.default_max_attempts.help: How many times a deployment tries a machine before giving up. An attempt is spent when the install fails OR when the machine never picks the command up.

deploy.default_retry_backoff_seconds.label: Default retry backoff
deploy.default_retry_backoff_seconds.help: Wait before the first retry. It doubles each attempt (15 min, 30 min, 1 h...), so a machine that's off for the weekend isn't retried every quarter hour.

deploy.max_upload_mb.label: Largest package file
deploy.max_upload_mb.help: Upload limit for a hub-hosted installer. Files are stored beside the database and shared between packages built from the same installer.

deploy.scheduler_interval_seconds.label: Run the deploy scheduler every
deploy.scheduler_interval_seconds.help: How often the hub checks for deployments that are due and reads finished attempts back. Also the floor on how quickly a scheduled window starts.

backup.hub_enabled.label: Back up the hub database on a schedule
backup.hub_enabled.help: Off until you have created a destination and stored the encryption key somewhere other than this server. Nothing is uploaded while this is off.

backup.hub_destination.label: Back up to
backup.hub_destination.help: The id of the destination scheduled backups are written to. Set this from the Backups page, which offers the configured destinations by name -- this field is the raw id it writes.

backup.hub_interval_hours.label: Back up every
backup.hub_interval_hours.help: Measured from the last ATTEMPT, not the last success -- a destination that has been down for a week is retried on this cadence rather than on every scheduler tick.

backup.hub_keep_generations.label: Keep this many backups
backup.hub_keep_generations.help: After a successful upload, older backups beyond this count are DELETED from the destination. At the default daily cadence this is two weeks of history. Counted from what the destination actually holds, so a file you delete by hand is not silently replaced.

backup.files_enabled.label: Back up files on managed PCs
backup.files_enabled.help: Off until you have chosen a destination and reviewed the included paths. Individual machines can opt out (or in) on their own Backup tab.

backup.files_destination.label: Back up PC files to
backup.files_destination.help: The id of the destination per-PC backups are written to. Set this from the Backups page; each machine gets its own folder under it.

backup.files_include.label: Include these paths
backup.files_include.help: Tokens expand on each machine: %Users% (or %User%) covers every real profile -- %User%\Scripts backs up everyone's Scripts folder -- and %Desktop%/%Documents% follow OneDrive folder redirection -- which a literal C:\Users\name\Desktop does not, so it would back up an empty stub on any PC using Known Folder Move.

backup.files_exclude.label: Never back up these
backup.files_exclude.help: Matched against the full path, case-insensitively. A pattern with no backslash matches on filename anywhere; ** crosses folders. Excluding a folder also excludes everything inside it.

backup.files_interval_hours.label: Back up PC files every
backup.files_interval_hours.help: Measured from the last attempt on each machine, so a laptop that was off is picked up when it returns rather than skipped.

backup.files_full_every.label: Take a full backup every
backup.files_full_every.help: Runs in between upload only files that changed. A shorter chain restores faster and survives a damaged archive better; a longer one uses less bandwidth.

backup.files_keep_chains.label: Keep this many backup chains
backup.files_keep_chains.help: A chain is one full backup plus the incrementals that follow it. Whole chains are deleted together -- never a full on its own, which would strand every incremental depending on it.

backup.files_max_file_mb.label: Skip files larger than
backup.files_max_file_mb.help: Skipped files are named in the run result rather than failing the run. Stops one forgotten disk image from consuming a night's upload.

backup.files_max_set_gb.label: Abort a run larger than
backup.files_max_set_gb.help: A safety stop: if the selected paths add up to more than this, the run fails with a message instead of uploading for two days. Raise it deliberately rather than by accident.

backup.files_use_vss.label: Use a shadow copy (VSS)
backup.files_use_vss.help: Reads from a point-in-time snapshot so files that are open -- an Outlook PST, a document someone left up -- are captured consistently. If a snapshot cannot be created the run continues against the live filesystem and reports which files were locked.

backup.files_max_concurrent.label: Back up at most this many PCs at once
backup.files_max_concurrent.help: Machines that were offline are backed up as soon as they return, so a Monday morning can bring the whole fleet back at once. This spreads them out instead of saturating the connection. Others wait their turn and start within a minute of a slot freeing up; 0 removes the limit.

remote.enabled.label: Allow remote view/control
remote.enabled.help: Master switch for starting remote sessions from a machine's Remote tab. Off means the Start button is refused fleet-wide, regardless of who holds the remote_control capability.

remote.consent_mode.label: Consent mode
remote.consent_mode.help: Unattended connects immediately (standard RMM). Attended prompts the logged-in user to approve first, and does nothing if no one is signed in. A per-machine override lives on the machine's Remote tab.

remote.session_ttl_seconds.label: End a session automatically after
remote.session_ttl_seconds.help: A remote session is force-ended past this age even if the tab is still open, which also bounds how long a minted TURN credential stays valid. Four hours by default.

remote.turn_ttl_seconds.label: TURN credential lifetime
remote.turn_ttl_seconds.help: How long the short-lived TURN credentials handed to each peer stay valid. Only needs to cover connection setup; media keeps flowing once ICE completes.

remote.stun_urls.label: STUN servers
remote.stun_urls.help: STUN URLs offered to both peers for NAT discovery, e.g. stun:stun.l.google.com:19302. Optional; leave empty on a LAN. One entry is enough -- a STUN URL on a LAN address just returns a peer its own LAN address, duplicating a candidate it already has.

remote.turn_urls.label: TURN servers
remote.turn_urls.help: TURN relay URLs, tried in order. Required for peers behind NATs that block direct connections. A relay behind NAT needs three: turn:PUBLIC-HOST:3478 for peers on the internet, turn:LAN-IP:3478 for a peer inside the relay's own network, and turn:LAN-IP:3479 for two peers both inside it -- see turn/README.md. Credentials are minted per session from REMOTE_TURN_SECRET in .env; TURN is skipped if that secret is unset.

directory.enabled.label: Sync with Active Directory
directory.enabled.help: Read computer objects from an on-prem domain controller so machines carry their OU, owner and AD name. Off by default; nothing contacts a DC until this is on and the fields below are filled in.

directory.server.label: Domain controller URL
directory.server.help: e.g. ldaps://dc1.corp.local. Use ldaps:// (port 636) -- a plain ldap:// bind sends the service account's password in cleartext and is refused unless you explicitly allow it below.

directory.base_dn.label: Search base
directory.base_dn.help: Where to search for computer objects, e.g. OU=Computers,DC=corp,DC=local. Narrow this to the OU your managed PCs live in rather than the domain root: it is faster and it keeps servers and other objects out of the results.

directory.bind_dn.label: Bind account
directory.bind_dn.help: A READ-ONLY service account, e.g. CN=fleethub,OU=Service,DC=corp,DC=local (a user@corp.local UPN also works). Its password goes in .env as DIRECTORY_BIND_PASSWORD. Nothing here ever writes to the directory.

directory.computer_filter.label: LDAP filter
directory.computer_filter.help: The LDAP filter for computer objects. Narrow it to exclude servers or stale accounts, e.g. (&(objectClass=computer)(!(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=2)))  to skip disabled ones.

directory.sync_interval_minutes.label: Sync every
directory.sync_interval_minutes.help: How often to re-read the directory. Hourly is plenty -- OUs change rarely, and every pass is a full read of the search base.

directory.page_size.label: LDAP page size
directory.page_size.help: Results per page. Searches are always paged; AD's default server limit is 1000 and it truncates silently rather than erroring, which would look like half the fleet vanishing from the directory.

directory.timeout_seconds.label: Connection timeout
directory.timeout_seconds.help: How long to wait for the domain controller before giving up on a pass.

directory.alert_on_unmatched.label: Alert on machines missing from AD
directory.alert_on_unmatched.help: Raise a review alert for a managed machine the directory has no computer object for -- usually a PC that was never domain-joined, was renamed, or is half-decommissioned. Auto-resolves when the machine reappears.

directory.tls_verify.label: Verify the DC's certificate
directory.tls_verify.help: Validate the domain controller's LDAPS certificate. Turn off only for a lab with a self-signed cert -- with it off, anything that can intercept the connection can capture the service account's password.

directory.allow_insecure.label: Allow plain (unencrypted) LDAP
directory.allow_insecure.help: Permit binding over ldap:// without TLS. The bind password is then sent in CLEARTEXT across your network. Leave off unless this is an isolated lab.

firmware.max_upload_mb.label: Largest firmware image
firmware.max_upload_mb.help: Upload limit for a BIOS image. Images are stored beside the database in their own folder, so a package clean-up can never remove one.

firmware.scheduler_interval_seconds.label: Run the firmware scheduler every
firmware.scheduler_interval_seconds.help: How often the hub sends out firmware updates that are due, and closes out machines that never reported back.

firmware.flashing_timeout_seconds.label: Give up on a running flash after
firmware.flashing_timeout_seconds.help: How long a machine may hold a fetched image without reporting. Reaching this is recorded as a failure that may have left the machine mid-flash, so check it before trying again.

firmware.confirm_timeout_seconds.label: Wait for the new BIOS version for
firmware.confirm_timeout_seconds.help: A flash finishes during startup, so it is confirmed only when the machine reports its new BIOS version. Keep this generous: a PC flashed on a Friday evening is confirmed on Monday morning.

firmware.require_ac_power.label: Require mains power to flash
firmware.require_ac_power.help: A laptop that loses power mid-flash may not start again. The agent refuses the update while it is running on battery.

firmware.min_battery_percent.label: Minimum battery charge to flash
firmware.min_battery_percent.help: Checked as well as mains power: a machine plugged in at the desk with a flat battery is still at risk if the power is pulled during the restart.

wake.scheduler_interval_seconds.label: Run the wake scheduler every
wake.scheduler_interval_seconds.help: How often the hub looks for a PC that can send a magic packet, and checks whether a woken PC has come back.

wake.request_ttl_seconds.label: Keep looking for a relay for
wake.request_ttl_seconds.help: A wake waits for an awake PC on the same subnet to send it. This bounds the wait, so a wake asked for on Friday evening does not fire on Monday morning.

wake.confirm_timeout_seconds.label: Wait for the PC to check in for
wake.confirm_timeout_seconds.help: Nothing acknowledges a magic packet, so a wake is confirmed only by the PC checking in. Reaching this is reported as no check-in yet, not as a failed wake.

wake.hub_broadcast.label: Let the hub send the packet itself
wake.hub_broadcast.help: Only used when no PC on the target's subnet is awake, and only when the hub is on that subnet. A hub broadcast never leaves the hub's own network segment, which is why another PC on the subnet is always tried first.

wake.auto_wake_targets.label: Wake PCs before a scheduled window runs
wake.auto_wake_targets.help: Deployments and firmware updates only reach PCs that are switched on. With this on, the hub wakes a window's offline targets when it opens.

hub.device_token_lifetime_days.label: Device access lifetime
hub.device_token_lifetime_days.help: How long a paired app keeps working without being used. Every use extends it. Devices already paired keep the lifetime they were paired with.

_choice: Labels for the enum settings whose vocabulary is FIXED in code. Enums whose
choices come from data (a backup destination id) are shown verbatim and have no
entries here -- an operator's own name for a bucket is not ours to translate.

remote.consent_mode.attended: Attended - ask the signed-in user first

_error: Validation messages, shown verbatim beside the offending field. Each is prefixed
with that field's own label by the caller, so write them to continue a sentence
that has already named the setting: 'Keep readings for: must be at least 1 day'.

error.bad_url_scheme: {value} must start with stun:, stuns:, turn: or turns:

settings.no_permission: You do not have permission to change settings.

directory.no_bind_password: No bind password is set. Add {var}=... to the hub's .env and restart -- it is a credential, so it is deliberately not stored in hub settings.
directory.enable_first: Turn the sync on above to run a pass.
directory.sync_result: Synced: {found} objects in AD, {matched} machines matched, {unmatched} not found in AD.
directory.duplicates: These hostnames have more than one computer object in AD; the first of each was used: {machines}

remote.title: TURN / STUN status
remote.cannot_write_env: This deployment cannot write .env from the hub; set REMOTE_TURN_SECRET on the host and restart the hub.
remote.secret_placeholder: Paste an existing coturn secret, or leave blank to generate
remote.secret_saved: Saved and applied to the hub. Copy it now -- it is not shown again. coturn validates against its OWN copy, so set the SAME value as its --static-auth-secret (turn/.env REMOTE_TURN_SECRET) and restart coturn, or TURN will reject every allocation.
remote.no_ice_warning: A session hands peers 0 ICE servers, so anything not on the same LAN fails to connect (the agent logs "ice_servers=0"). Add a STUN and/or TURN URL below and, for TURN, set the shared secret.
remote.urls_help: Point TURN servers at the hub's coturn, e.g. turn:your-hub:3478 (and stun:your-hub:3478). The URLs are the fields below; this secret is what mints per-session credentials.
remote.vdd_help: A machine with no monitor has no display output, so screen capture has nothing to duplicate and remote view shows a black screen. Upload the driver's "Driver Only" zip on the Packages page, then pin its SHA-256 here. Operators can then install it per machine from the Remote tab.
remote.vdd_sha_placeholder: SHA-256 of the uploaded package (64 hex characters)

signin.denied: Only the break-glass administrators listed in ALLOWED_EMAILS can change these. Whoever configures the identity provider decides who this hub believes you are, so it is deliberately not delegable through a permission group.
signin.env_note: These are written to the hub's .env and applied immediately — no restart. Client secrets are never shown again once saved.
signin.google_help: Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application) in the Google Cloud Console and add this hub's /auth/callback as an authorised redirect URI. Leave both fields empty to turn Google sign-in off.
signin.secret_saved: A secret is saved. Leave this untouched to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
signin.oidc_help: Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Authentik, Keycloak, Auth0 — any OIDC issuer. Register a confidential web application with this hub's /auth/oidc/callback as the redirect URI. Endpoints and signing keys come from discovery, so there is nothing vendor-specific to configure here.
signin.issuer_help: e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT-ID/v2.0 — the discovery URL is derived from this. Must be https.
signin.metadata_help: Only needed if your provider does not serve /.well-known/openid-configuration under the issuer. Clear it to have it re-derived from the issuer above.
signin.button_label_help: What the sign-in button says. "Microsoft" reads far better than "SSO" to somebody looking at an unfamiliar login page.
signin.scopes_help: Must include openid. Add "groups" (or your provider's equivalent) if you map directory groups to permission groups.
signin.no_provider_left: That would leave no way to sign in to this hub. Configure Google or an OIDC provider before saving.
signin.confirm:
Change how people sign in to this hub?

This takes effect immediately for new sign-ins. Existing sessions are not signed out. If the new settings are wrong, the break-glass administrators in ALLOWED_EMAILS can change them back — provided they can still sign in.

packages.heading: Packages
packages.intro: Describe an installer once -- payload, silent command line, and what proves it worked -- then deploy it to machines and watch it land.
packages.empty_hint: A package is an installer plus how to run it silently and how to tell it worked.
packages.confirm_delete: Delete the package "{package}"? Deployment history is kept.
packages.http_413: Upload rejected as too large (HTTP 413) before it reached the hub. This is the reverse proxy in front of the hub, not the hub's own limit -- raise client_max_body_size in nginx (or the equivalent: IIS maxAllowedContentLength, Apache LimitRequestBody) and reload it.
packages.http_502: The hub did not respond (HTTP {status}). A large upload can also hit the proxy's read timeout -- check the proxy log as well as the hub log.
_source: The four payload kinds a package can have. The KEY is the wire value and is fixed;
only label and help are shown. 'winget' is a product name and stays untranslated.

upload.label: Upload a file to the hub

unc.label: Copy from a UNC path
unc.help: The agent reads it from a share it can already reach.

editor.no_payloads: No payloads. A winget or PowerShell step may not need one.

editor.will_upload: {file} will be uploaded when you save.

editor.current_payload: Current payload: {file} ({size}). Choose a file to replace it.

editor.mode_command_help: One installer, one silent command line. Runs on every agent version.
editor.mode_steps_help: Unpack an archive, install drivers, run a script -- in order, each judged on its own. Needs agent 3.22.0 or newer.
editor.steps_help: Steps run top to bottom. The deploy stops at the first one that fails, unless you tell it to carry on.
editor.no_steps: No steps yet. Pick a kind below and add one.
editor.too_many_steps: A package may have at most {max} steps.
editor.pnputil_codes: blank = 0, 259, 3010 -- 259 is a driver install that simply ran out of INFs
editor.continue_on_error: Carry on even if this step fails
editor.dest_hint: blank = a folder in the working directory
editor.driver_path_hint: usually the folder an earlier unpack step produced
editor.cmd_help: Use {placeholder} where the downloaded payload goes — it must appear in the command or the arguments.
editor.cmd_help_winget: The agent builds the winget command line. Anything here is appended as extra switches.
editor.exit_codes_help: Comma separated. 3010 means "installed, reboot required" -- drop it only if you want a pending reboot to count as a failure.
editor.proof_help: An installer exiting 0 is evidence, not proof -- silent installers routinely return 0 having done nothing. This check runs after it and has to pass too.
editor.version_help: Matched against Windows' installed-programs list, in both the 64- and 32-bit registry views.

deploy_editor.title: Deploy package
deploy_editor.retry_help: An attempt is spent when the install fails or when the machine never picks the command up. The wait doubles each time.

deployments.empty_hint: Deploy a package from the Packages tab and its progress shows up here.
deployments.title: Deployment
deployments.confirm_cancel: Stop this deployment? Machines already running the installer will finish.

_status: Deployment and per-machine statuses. These are shown in tables and in the tally
under the progress bar, so keep them short.

GET /api/packages in the caller's language -- same discipline as the detection
kinds below, and the same test enforcing it.

run.label: Run a program
run.description: An executable with arguments: an MSI, a vendor setup.exe, anything already on the machine.

powershell.label: Run PowerShell
powershell.description: An inline script, run as SYSTEM. The catch-all -- copy a file, set a registry value, restart a service.

winget.label: Install with winget

extract.label: Unpack a .zip

pnputil.label: Install drivers
pnputil.description: Hands a folder of .inf files to pnputil, which stages and installs each one.

GET /api/packages in the caller's language. A kind added without entries here
fails tests/test_i18n.py rather than captioning the form with its own key.

none.label: No detection check
none.description: Trust the exit code alone. Only sensible for installers you know report failure honestly.

file_exists.label: File exists
file_exists.description: Succeed only if a path is present after the install, e.g. C:\Program Files\7-Zip\7z.exe.

registry_value.label: Registry value
registry_value.description: Succeed only if a registry value exists -- optionally matching an exact string.

installed_version.label: Installed version
installed_version.description: Look the product up in Windows' installed-programs registry and require at least a given version.

backups.heading: Backups
backups.intro: A consistent snapshot of the hub database, compressed, encrypted here, and pushed offsite on a schedule. The storage provider only ever sees ciphertext.

key.missing_library_text: The cryptography package is not installed, so backups cannot be encrypted or restored. Run: pip install -r requirements.txt, then restart the hub.
key.none_text: Backups are encrypted on this server before upload. Create the key to get started — you will be shown it once, and you must store it somewhere other than this machine.
key.unescrowed_title: The encryption key has never been stored anywhere else
key.unescrowed_text: If this server is lost, every backup it has taken becomes permanently unreadable. Reveal the key, store it in a password manager or a sealed envelope, and confirm.
key.ok_text: Key {id} — confirmed stored offline on {when}. Restore with restore_backup.py, which needs only this key and the backup file.
key.modal_warning: This key is the only thing that can decrypt your backups. It is not stored in the hub database, and it is not recoverable — if this server is lost and you have not written this down somewhere else, every backup ever taken becomes unreadable.
key.modal_store: Store it in a password manager or a sealed envelope — somewhere that does not depend on this machine. To restore, you need this key and the backup file, and nothing else:
key.copied: Copied. Paste it somewhere durable before closing this.
key.copy_failed: Could not copy automatically — click the key to select it.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.no_destination: Add a destination first — there is nowhere to put a backup yet.
schedule.off: Nothing is uploaded while this is off.
schedule.due_now: Due now — the next scheduler pass will take it.
schedule.rotation_note: Older backups beyond that count are deleted from the destination after each successful upload.

runs.title: Recent backups
runs.empty_hint: Press "Back up now" to take one immediately, or turn the schedule on.

files.title: What gets backed up on managed PCs
files.intro: Applies to every machine unless that machine overrides it on its own Backup tab. Paths are expanded on each PC, so one pattern covers everyone — including people who sign in for the first time next week.
files.enabled: Back up files on managed PCs
files.on_note: Machines are backed up on the schedule below.
files.off_note: Nothing on any PC is backed up while this is off.
files.max_concurrent: Back up at most (PCs at once)
files.vss_note: Captures files that are open, like an Outlook PST.
files.include_help: A folder to back up. Use %Users% (or %User%) to cover every profile, or %Desktop% to follow each user's real Desktop even when OneDrive has redirected it.
files.exclude_help: Matched against the whole path, case-insensitively. A pattern with no backslash matches on filename anywhere; ** crosses folders. Excluding a folder also excludes everything inside it.

fleet_run.title: Back up now
fleet_run.intro: Asks every PC you can see to back up, without waiting for its next scheduled run. Machines that are switched off are not skipped — each one backs up the moment it comes online again.
fleet_run.stopped_in_flight: {count} already uploading (will finish, then be discarded)
fleet_run.queued: {count} queued (offline or waiting for a free slot)
fleet_run.none_configured: No machines are set up to back up yet.

preview.title: Preview
preview.intro: What these patterns resolve to on a real machine, using the profiles its agent last reported. This is the only way to see that a folder is redirected into OneDrive before a restore comes up empty.
preview.choose_machine: Choose a machine to see what these patterns actually cover on it.
preview.no_profiles: {machine} has not reported its user profiles yet — its agent sends them on the next heartbeat after an upgrade. Until then these patterns cannot be resolved here; they will still expand correctly on the machine.
preview.covers_nothing: These patterns cover nothing on this machine.

exceptions.title: Machines with their own settings
exceptions.none: Every machine follows the settings above. Override one from its own Backup tab.

destinations.empty_hint: A destination is an S3-compatible bucket or a WebDAV share. Credentials are encrypted on this server and never shown again.
destinations.confirm_delete: Delete destination "{name}"? Backups already uploaded to it are NOT deleted, but the hub will no longer be able to reach them.

editor.name: Name
editor.path_style_help: On for MinIO and most self-hosted gateways (host/bucket/key); off for AWS (bucket.host/key). Getting it wrong shows up as a signature error, not a 404.
editor.keep_credentials: Leave both blank to keep the stored credentials unchanged.
editor.new_credentials: Stored encrypted on this server with the backup master key. Never shown again.

_kind: One label + description per entry in backups.DESTINATION_KINDS, served by
GET /api/backups in the caller's language. Product names (S3, WebDAV, MinIO) stay

s3.label: S3-compatible
s3.description: AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi -- anything speaking the S3 API. Signed with SigV4; the hub can also mint scoped upload URLs from it.

webdav.label: WebDAV
webdav.description: Nextcloud, ownCloud, IIS, or any WebDAV share. Authenticated with a username and password over HTTPS.

_token: The %Token% names themselves are the grammar and are NOT translated -- they are what
an operator types. Only the explanation beside each one is.

token.users: Every real user profile on the machine (skips Public, Default and service accounts). One pattern covers everyone, including people who sign in for the first time next week.
token.user: The same as %Users% -- one path per real profile. Reads better for a custom subfolder: %User%\Scripts backs up every user's Scripts folder. It does NOT mean 'whoever is logged in now'; backups run with nobody signed in, so every per-user token covers all of them.
token.desktop: Each user's actual Desktop -- follows OneDrive folder redirection, unlike a literal C:\Users\name\Desktop.

tab.follow_on: Following the fleet policy: this machine IS backed up.
tab.follow_off: Following the fleet policy: nothing on this machine is backed up.
tab.override_on: Overridden: this machine is backed up even if the fleet policy is off.
tab.override_off: Overridden: this machine is NOT backed up, even though the fleet policy is on.
tab.extra_include_help: ADDED to the fleet list below, not replacing it. Use it for something only this PC has — a local project folder, a line-of-business data directory.
tab.extra_exclude_help: Also added to the fleet exclusions.

tab.other_machine_help: Another machine, if you are replacing this one. It needs to be in your scope too, and its agent does the work.
tab.write_to_placeholder: e.g. C:\Restored — blank means the original locations

Restore {count} item(s) back to their ORIGINAL locations on {machine}?

Files there will be replaced{qualifier}

confirm.end_many: This ends all {count} instances of {name} on {machine}. Anything unsaved in them is lost.

firmware.title: Firmware settings
firmware.refresh_title: Ask the machine to read its firmware settings again
firmware.refresh_queued: Queued. The machine reads its firmware on its next check-in and this page updates once it reports back.
firmware._state: Four states, and the first two are NOT the same claim: 'unknown' means nobody has told us yet, 'unsupported' means the machine told us it has nothing to manage.
firmware.unknown_help: This machine has not reported its firmware settings yet. It needs an agent that supports firmware inventory; one will arrive on its next check-in after the agent updates.
firmware.unsupported_help: This machine has no manageable firmware interface. Virtual machines and self-built PCs report this, and it is the expected, permanent answer for them rather than a fault.
firmware.error_unknown: The machine has a firmware interface but reading it failed, and it did not say why.
firmware._error_from_machine: Explains why an error can appear in a language the console is not set to. The message is Windows' own text on the reporting machine, so it arrives in that machine's language; translating it would mean inventing words the machine never said.
firmware.error_from_machine: This message comes from Windows on that machine, so it appears in that machine's language rather than yours.
firmware.password_set: A BIOS setup password is set on this machine. Changing a setting will need that password.
firmware._kind: How a value may be written. Shown because it is what an operator can do with the row, not vendor trivia.
firmware._write: Nothing here ever tells an operator to reboot on the strength of the vendor. A change is confirmed by re-reading the attribute, so only the pending_reboot state -- which means the firmware still reports the old value -- asks for a restart.
firmware.apply_queued: Queued. The machine applies the change on its next check-in, then reads each setting back so the result says what actually changed.
firmware.locked: A change is in flight for this machine. Settings can be edited again once it finishes.

change.reboot_help: The machine accepted the change, but its firmware still reports the old value. Restart it to apply.
change.observed: The firmware now reports {value}, which is neither value.

firmware.password_help: On every vendor a BIOS setup password blocks firmware changes. Stored encrypted and sent only to the machine making the change; it is never shown again.
firmware.password_required: Enter a password, or use Clear to remove the stored one.
firmware.password_ready: A BIOS setup password is set on this machine, and one is stored here to send with a change.
firmware.password_unknown: This machine's firmware does not say whether a setup password is set. If a change is refused, that is the first thing to check.
firmware.no_updates: This machine has not been sent a firmware update.

firmware.heading: Firmware updates
firmware.intro: Upload a vendor's BIOS image once, say which hardware it belongs to, and flash it onto machines.
firmware.warning_title: A firmware update cannot be undone
firmware.warning_body: Everything else here can be put back: a backup restored, a package reinstalled, a setting written again. A failed flash cannot. The hub refuses to send an image to a machine whose manufacturer and model it does not match, and the machine checks again before it writes — but nothing recovers a board that was interrupted mid-flash.
firmware.images_help: The models an image lists are what the hub matches a machine against. Take them from the vendor's own compatibility list.
firmware.jobs_help: A flash is confirmed when the machine comes back reporting the new BIOS version, not when the update tool exits.
firmware.no_jobs: No firmware updates have been sent yet.
firmware.confirm_delete: Delete the image {name}? Machines already updated with it are unaffected.
firmware.confirm_cancel_job: Cancel this update? Machines that have already been handed the image will finish flashing.
firmware.cancel_partial: {count} machine(s) had already been handed the image and will finish flashing.

editor.title: Add a firmware image
editor.file_hint: The vendor's own update executable. Up to {mb} MB.
editor.name: Name
editor.to_version_help: Exactly as the machine will report it afterwards. This is how the hub tells an applied flash from a failed one, so a machine that comes back on any other version is reported as unconfirmed rather than updated.
editor.models_help: Comma-separated, spelled as the machine reports its model. A machine whose model is not on this list is refused before anything is sent to it.
editor.args_help: Whatever makes the vendor's tool run silently. Leave blank to use the defaults the agent knows for that manufacturer.

flash.title: Flash firmware
flash.machines_help: Machines the image does not fit are listed back with the reason instead of being quietly skipped.
flash.window_help: Leave both empty to start as soon as each machine is online. A machine that is off keeps its turn rather than being marked failed.

_target: One entry per wire value of a firmware target's state -- resolved through a literal
lookup so tests/test_i18n.py's key scan can see them. 'refused' is deliberately not
a failure word: the image simply is not for that hardware, and nothing went wrong.

pair.heading: Pair a device
pair.intro: You are about to give an app on this device access to FleetHub as you. Check what it is being allowed to do before you confirm.
pair.expires_in_days: Access expires after {days} days without use, and can be revoked at any time from the Users page.
pair.capabilities_help: A device can never do more than you can. If your own permissions change later, this device follows them.
pair.forbidden: Managing settings, users, permission groups and firmware stays in the console and cannot be granted to a device.
pair.redirect_refused: This app's return address was refused
pair.redirect_refused_help: You can still pair by confirming below and typing the code into the app.
pair.pick_one: Choose at least one thing this device may do.
pair.handing_over: Handing the code to the app…
pair.code_help: Type this into the app within {seconds} seconds. It works once.

devices.heading: Paired devices
devices.intro: Every app signed in to this hub. Revoking a device stops it working immediately; it does not change anyone's permissions.
devices.empty_hint: A device appears here after somebody pairs the FleetHub app from the Download Client page.
devices.confirm_revoke: Revoke {device}? The app will stop working at once.

download.heading: Download the FleetHub client
download.intro: The native app for watching this fleet, with alerts and Wake-on-LAN. Install it, then pair it from the app.
